## 1. Characterising which tetravalent graphs are flag graphs of maniplexes

A tetravalent graph is the flag graph of a rank‑4 maniplex precisely when its
edges admit a proper colouring by four colours in which each colour class is a
perfect matching and every pair of non‑adjacent colours decomposes the graph
into 4‑gons. We conjecture that a connected tetravalent graph carries such a
colouring if and only if it has a fixed‑point‑free automorphism structure whose
generators satisfy the string relations, and that this can be decided in
polynomial time in the number of vertices.
*The key insight is* that the "string" (4‑gon) condition on non‑adjacent colour
classes is a purely local constraint, so admissibility should be checkable by a
local‑to‑global colour‑propagation argument rather than a global search.
*Why now?* Complete censuses of small tetravalent graphs now exist, giving a
finite testbed on which the local characterisation can be exhaustively confirmed
or refuted before attempting the general theorem.

## 2. Even‑order refinement: the flag count modulo higher powers of two

Every rank‑4 maniplex has an even number of flags because each colour is a
fixed‑point‑free involution. We conjecture a sharper statement: the flag count of
a rank‑4 maniplex is always divisible by eight, and by twenty‑four when the
maniplex is regular, with the residue class recording how many colour pairs are
adjacent versus non‑adjacent.
*The key insight is* that four independent perfect matchings plus the 4‑gon
structure of non‑adjacent pairs force nested two‑to‑one pairings of the flags,
compounding the factor of two.
*Why now?* The base evenness result is settled, so the natural next step is to
pin down the exact power of two, and the small‑case data (flag counts
120, 384, 1152, 14400, all divisible by twenty‑four) already suggests the target.

For non‑adjacent colour pairs the two matchings bound 4‑gons; for adjacent pairs
they bound `2p`‑gons where `p` is a Schläfli‑type parameter. We conjecture that
the multiset of these polygon sizes, together with the 4‑gon closure for
non‑adjacent pairs, is a complete isomorphism invariant for *regular* rank‑4
maniplexes — i.e. two regular 4‑maniplexes are isomorphic iff their colour‑pair
polygon data agree.
*The key insight is* that regularity makes the connection group act freely and
transitively, so the entire object is reconstructible from the finitely many
local relations among the four generators.
*Why now?* The 4‑gon result for non‑adjacent pairs is now proved, providing the
first coordinate of the proposed invariant and a template for the adjacent‑pair
polygons.

The rank‑4 flag graph is 4‑valent because there are four connection involutions.

lattices for small `N` to test the growth conjecture.
